engagement.judgement: Opening entry. The system the class went into prostate patients on is the tissue-agnostic BRCA2-null model of Bryant and Farmer 2005 (doi 10.1038/nature03445); no prostate-specific BRCA2 model preceded TOPARP.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Mixed-tumour phase 1 (22 BRCA carriers with ovarian, breast or prostate cancer); PD in any dosed human counts for engagement, as healthy volunteers would.
engagement.population: Phase 1, 60 patients incl. 22 BRCA1/2 carriers with ovarian, breast or prostate cancer, NCT00516373 (no results posted)
engagement.model: BRCA2-null synthetic lethality: BRCA2-deficient V-C8 and ES cells and V-C8 xenografts killed by PARP inhibition alone (Bryant 2005, Farmer 2005); tissue-agnostic, no prostate line
engagement.note: Olaparib inhibited PARP in patient PBMCs, hair follicles and tumour; responses only in BRCA carriers, prostate included.
engagement.short: PARP inhibited in patient PBMCs and tumour
engagement.quote: pharmacodynamic studies confirmed PARP inhibition in surrogate samples (of peripheral-blood mononuclear cells and plucked eyebrow-hair follicles) and tumor tissue.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me. The prostate trials (TOPARP, PROfound, MAGNITUDE, TALAPRO-2) reported no PAR pharmacodynamics, so the class-level PD read stays the 2009 phase 1.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the abstract does not name the inhibitor (veliparib, ABT-888, in the full paper as I recall it, so not a member). Asim 2017 and Li 2017 (doi 10.1126/scisignal.aam7479) repeated the in-vivo synergy with olaparib.

engagement.quote: In vivo analyses show that PARP-1 activity is required for AR function in xenograft tumors, as well as tumor cell growth in vivo and generation and maintenance of castration resistance.
engagement.judgement: Schiewer 2012, Asim 2017 (doi 10.1038/s41467-017-00393-y) and Li 2017 are three model programs with one prediction - PARP inhibitor plus AR blockade works without HRR selection - so one track. No trial read AR output or PAR on the combination, so untested, not empty.

dose.judgement: Dose follows efficacy (reached, worked). Niraparib's combination dose fell to 200 mg (BEDIVERE RP2D, below the 300 mg monotherapy dose) and talazoparib's to 0.5 mg with enzalutamide, for tolerability and a P-gp interaction, but both regimens worked in BRCA patients (Chi 2023; Agarwal 2023), so no toxicity block under decision 16; the model stated no margin.

dose.confidence_note: Bundle text of the 2014 clinical pharmacology review, Appendix 3.3 (PBPK review). An in-silico clinical-pharmacology model, not an efficacy model; its own track because it is a different system with a different prediction (exposure under CYP3A modulation).
dose.judgement: Opening entry at first regulatory use (2014 capsule NDA 206162, ovarian). The model was verified against DDI studies already run; the retrodiction flag sits on the retro entry, not the opener (lint).
dose.population: Simcyp olaparib PBPK model; capsule 400 mg BID; simulations for itraconazole, rifampin, fluconazole and efavirenz

Cross-indication PK admitted under the healthy-volunteer PK rule; the same DDI dose modifications carry on the 2020 mCRPC label. The dose rule's 'enough' half is untested: efficacy at DDI-reduced doses was never trialled.
dose.reason: Reproduced observed CYP3A DDI, inducer under-predicted
dose.judgement: Retro under decision 10: FDA 'verified' the model against clinical DDI studies already run, so it reproduces rather than predicts. Itraconazole within 2x, rifampin off 2.7x in the right direction, and FDA answered 'Yes' on adequacy: partial. The fluconazole and efavirenz predictions that set the moderate-modulator doses were never tested in patients, so no prospective entry follows.
dose.magnitude_basis: PBPK-predicted vs observed olaparib AUC ratio: itraconazole 2.75 vs 2.66, rifampin 0.32 vs 0.12 (2.7-fold)

efficacy.reason: Unselected synergy failed in HRR-negative cohort
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: two of three all-comer phase 3s (PROpel, TALAPRO-2) met their primaries, but the only trial that prospectively enrolled an HRR-negative cohort and tested it on its own was stopped for futility, and the FDA confined all three combinations to BRCA- or HRR-mutated disease (Akeega review; 2023 Lynparza and Talzenna labels). Under the track rule one drug's contra beats another's same; endpoint_role poc_gate because the futility gate, not rPFS, decided the cohort.

efficacy.model: LuCaP PDX-derived organoid platform: olaparib dose-response across BRCA2 wild-type, single-copy-loss (LuCaP 86.2) and two-copy-loss (LuCaP 86.2CR) mCRPC organoids (Beshiri 2018)
efficacy.note: LuCaP PDX-derived organoids tested for olaparib sensitivity by BRCA2 genotype; prediction is which genotype responds.
efficacy.short: LuCaP organoids: olaparib by BRCA2 genotype
efficacy.quote: The utility of the platform as a genotype-dependent model of drug sensitivity was tested with olaparib and carboplatin.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC6125202). model_kind ex_vivo: patient-derived tumour passaged as PDX and assayed as organoids in vitro; the enum has no PDX-organoid value.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at first use; the comparison is in the same paper and is scored as the next entry. The paper was written knowing TOPARP-A; the retrodiction flag sits on the retro entry, not the opener (lint).
efficacy.population: LuCaP PDX-derived organoid lines of three BRCA2 genotypes: wild-type, single-copy loss (LuCaP 86.2), two-copy loss (LuCaP 86.2CR)

efficacy.model: LuCaP PDX-derived organoid platform: olaparib dose-response across BRCA2 wild-type, single-copy-loss (LuCaP 86.2) and two-copy-loss (LuCaP 86.2CR) mCRPC organoids (Beshiri 2018)
efficacy.note: BRCA2 two-copy-loss LuCaP 86.2CR organoids >100-fold more olaparib-sensitive than hemizygous or wild-type lines; paper pairs this with TOPARP-A BRCA2 responders.
efficacy.quote: Finally, we observed maximum cytotoxicity to the PARP inhibitor olaparib in BRCA2-/- organoids, similar to responses observed in patients.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. The patient side is TOPARP-A's published genotype-level result, not the organoid donors' own outcomes; the LuCaP 86.2/86.2CR donor was never treated with olaparib. Only olaparib tested; IC50 0.48 uM (86.2CR) vs 65.0 uM (86.2).
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction under decision 10: the experiment is framed 'To compare organoids to genotype-determined patient responses' citing TOPARP-A (2015), so the match is retro, never same. Patient-level track: the prediction is which BRCA2 genotype responds. magnitude direction_only because organoid IC50 and patient time to progression are different quantities.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: Organoid olaparib IC50 by BRCA2 genotype (0.48 vs 65.0 uM, >100-fold) against TOPARP-A response by BRCA2 status: different quantities, direction only
efficacy.population: LuCaP 86.2 (BRCA2 hemizygous), LuCaP 86.2CR (BRCA2 two-copy loss) and BRCA2-wild-type LuCaP organoids vs TOPARP-A BRCA2-loss mCRPC patients (Mateo 2015)

patient_trials.quote: Treatment with the PARP inhibitor olaparib in patients whose prostate cancers were no longer responding to standard treatments and who had defects in DNA-repair genes led to a high response rate.

safety.magnitude_basis: Hematopoietic target organ in rats and dogs vs anaemia, neutropenia and thrombocytopenia in patients; exposures 2-4% of clinical
safety.confidence_note: Full review passage read. Comparison made in ovarian cancer patients (imported); the olaparib prostate population came later.
safety.population: Rats and dogs, 26-week studies; ovarian cancer patients on olaparib 400 mg BID (imported)
safety.model: Rat and dog repeat-dose toxicology of olaparib, niraparib and talazoparib: hematopoietic system the major target organ (FDA nonclinical reviews)
safety.note: Rats and dogs on olaparib: marrow atrophy with falling red cells and leukocytes at 2-4% of clinical exposure; FDA calls it consistent with patients.
safety.quote: In general toxicology studies, the major target organ of toxicity was the hematopoietic system, which is consistent with adverse reactions reported in patients treated with olaparib.
safety.judgement: No untested opener: the first public description of the toxicology and the first comparison are the same FDA document. Imported from ovarian cancer under the safety transfer rule; the prostate datum is the 2023 entry.

safety.magnitude_basis: Marrow depletion in rats and dogs vs anaemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia at 300 mg daily in patients
safety.confidence_note: Full review passage read; comparison made in ovarian cancer (NOVA), imported. The same review records niraparib binding DAT (IC50 63 nM) and raising blood pressure and heart rate in vagotomised dogs, the secondary pharmacology behind the hypertension later seen in MAGNITUDE.
safety.population: Rats and dogs, 90-day studies; ovarian cancer patients on niraparib 300 mg daily (imported)
safety.model: Rat and dog repeat-dose toxicology of olaparib, niraparib and talazoparib: hematopoietic system the major target organ (FDA nonclinical reviews)
safety.note: Niraparib: rat deaths from marrow toxicity, dog reticulocyte falls; FDA states the hematopoietic findings matched the frequent clinical events.
safety.quote: Thus, toxicological findings in the hematopoietic system in nonclinical studies were consistent with the frequent adverse events observed in clinical trials.
safety.judgement: Strengthens with a second member drug; talazoparib's 2018 review (NDA 211651) makes the same statement for a third.

safety.magnitude_basis: Marrow depletion in rats and dogs vs grade 3-4 anaemia 28% in prostate patients on niraparib 200 mg with abiraterone
safety.confidence_note: Label read in full for this section; Talzenna 2024 label gives TALAPRO-2 grade 3+ anaemia 45%, neutropenia 18%, thrombocytopenia 8%.
safety.population: MAGNITUDE Cohort 1, HRR-mutated mCRPC, niraparib 200 mg + AAP, NCT03748641
safety.model: Rat and dog repeat-dose toxicology of olaparib, niraparib and talazoparib: hematopoietic system the major target organ (FDA nonclinical reviews)
safety.note: Prostate: MAGNITUDE grade 3-4 anaemia 28%, 27% transfused; TALAPRO-2 grade 3+ anaemia 45%; the marrow prediction held in this disease.
safety.quote: In MAGNITUDE Cohort 1, Grade 3-4 anemia, thrombocytopenia, and neutropenia were reported, respectively in 28%, 8%, and 7% of patients receiving AKEEGA.
safety.reason: Rat/dog marrow prediction held in prostate
safety.judgement: Paired by me (the label does not cite the toxicology). MDS/AML (0.4% in TALAPRO-2) was not a stated animal prediction and no carcinogenicity study was run, so it is not askable silence and is not scored.

safety.confidence_note: Imported from the breast-cancer PARP tile (decision 12, safety only); its drafter read the full text and found body weight the only toxicity readout.
safety.model: Pamiparib's own BRCA1-mutant MDA-MB-436 TNBC xenograft with tumour PAR pharmacodynamics and a mouse PK/PD model (head-to-head vs olaparib)
safety.note: Xenograft study reported no effect on body weight at any dose; haematology not measured; no patient comparison yet.
safety.quote: all treatments had no effect on mouse body weight
safety.judgement: Opening entry carried over from the breast tile; tolerability stated on body weight alone, so the haematology question is askable silence.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level on the patient side; imported from the breast-cancer PARP tile (decision 12). Pamiparib has no prostate trial.
safety.population: gBRCA1/2-mutated HER2-negative advanced breast cancer (China), NCT03575065 (imported)
safety.model: Pamiparib's own BRCA1-mutant MDA-MB-436 TNBC xenograft with tumour PAR pharmacodynamics and a mouse PK/PD model (head-to-head vs olaparib)
safety.note: Pamiparib monotherapy in gBRCA breast cancer: haematologic grade 3+ events common, 65% dose-reduced; the mouse that could show cytopenias reported none.
safety.quote: The most common treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs), treatment-related TEAEs, and ≥ Grade 3 TEAEs were hematologic (including anemia, decreased neutrophil count, and decreased white blood cell count).
safety.judgement: Imported safety comparison for a member drug (decision 12). A mouse can show marrow suppression and the study measured only body weight, so its 'no effect' is askable silence contradicted by patients; counted here, not in dose, because the model never predicted the harm (decision 16). Kept on its own track because the toxicology species did predict the harm.
